review_notes:
I read all 112 lines of the target file. I also checked the definitions it relies on in RealPolynomialChartSubstitution.lean: polynomialFirstJetHom, polynomialFirstJet_base (@[simp]), polynomialFirstJet_coord, polynomialLogDerivative, dualEvalLie_base and dualEvalLie_tangent. I checked NilpotentLieBCHGroup.map in BCHNonlinearRemainder.lean and the map_coord lemma (rfl, not simp) in DualIdealSteps.lean.

The file declares no simp lemmas itself. The one concrete simp-interface gap shows up as a repeated pattern. Six times, a proof uses `change` to manually unfold the expression `dualBaseLinear/dualTangentLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord` into `... (dualEvalLie t h P.coord)` and then calls `rw [dualEvalLie_base/_tangent]`. This happens because nothing rewrites that expression to its normal form `eval t P.coord` or `eval t (directionalDerivative h P.coord)`. The existing polynomialFirstJet_coord is not simp and rewrites to a different form: a sum of dualConstantLie and dualInfinitesimal. The base fact exists only at group level (polynomialFirstJet_base, which is about dualBaseHom), not for the underlying coordinate.

The `simpa only [polynomialFirstJet_base, polynomialLogDerivative]` transfers on lines 58, 61 and 105 unfold the definition on both sides. That works, and I don't consider it a defect. I have not compiled the proposed lemmas. I believe the `.coord` equality holds by `rfl`, because the existing `change` calls and map_coord are both definitional, but this is unverified.

findings.excerpt:
have haU : dualBaseLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h A).coord ∈ U := by
    change dualBaseLinear (dualEvalLie t h A.coord) ∈ U
    rw [dualEvalLie_base]
findings.problem: No simp or rewrite lemma brings `dualBaseLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord` or `dualTangentLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord` to its natural normal form, `eval t P.coord` or `eval t (directionalDerivative h P.coord)`. So each of the four `have`s (haU, hcU, haV, hcV) first uses `change` to unfold `polynomialFirstJetHom`/`NilpotentLieBCHGroup.map` definitionally and only then rewrites. The existing `polynomialFirstJet_base` is @[simp], but it applies only at group level (`dualBaseHom (...)`), not to the `.coord` projection that these goals contain. `polynomialFirstJet_coord` is not simp and expands to a `dualConstantLie + dualInfinitesimal` sum instead of the projected values.
findings.proposed_change:
In RealPolynomialChartSubstitution.lean, next to polynomialFirstJet_base, add:
`@[simp] theorem dualBaseLinear_polynomialFirstJet_coord (t h) (P : PolynomialGroup σ hnil) : dualBaseLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord = eval t P.coord := dualEvalLie_base t h P.coord`
and
`@[simp] theorem dualTangentLinear_polynomialFirstJet_coord [Fintype σ] (t h) (P) : dualTangentLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord = eval t (directionalDerivative h P.coord) := dualEvalLie_tangent t h P.coord`.
The definitional step is the one the current `change` already relies on, so the proofs should go through. Each `change … ; rw [dualEvalLie_base]` pair then becomes `rw [dualBaseLinear_polynomialFirstJet_coord]` (or `simp only [...]`).
findings.benefit: This removes four fragile `change` steps that restate the full goal and depend on how polynomialFirstJetHom unfolds. Rewriting the projection to `eval` gives simp a canonical target for this expression, so later membership arguments about the first-jet coordinates can use `simp`/`rw` directly instead of copying the unfolding.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp] theorem polynomialFirstJet_base (t h : σ → ℚ) (P : PolynomialGroup σ hnil) :
    dualBaseHom (polynomialFirstJetHom t h P) = polynomialValueHom t P := by

(polynomialFirstJetHom t h P).coord = dualConstantLie (eval t P.coord) +
      dualInfinitesimal (eval t (directionalDerivative h P.coord)) :=
dualTangentLinear (dualEvalLie t h p) = eval t (directionalDerivative h p) := by
(map (hM := hM) f g).coord = f g.coord := rfl

· change dualBaseLinear (dualEvalLie t h A.coord) ∈ U
    rw [dualEvalLie_base]
findings.problem: This is the same missing projection rewrite as in the previous finding. The two side goals produced by `dualLogDerivative_mem_of_invariant` mention `(polynomialFirstJetHom t h A).coord`, and with no lemma for its base or tangent projection, the proof again restates both goals with `change` before calling `dualEvalLie_base` and `dualEvalLie_tangent`. Here and in polynomial_removal_preserves_derivative_layers, the same two-step `change`/`rw` dance appears six times in total.
findings.proposed_change: Once `dualBaseLinear_polynomialFirstJet_coord` and `dualTangentLinear_polynomialFirstJet_coord` exist (as proposed above), replace the bullets with `rw [dualBaseLinear_polynomialFirstJet_coord]; exact (eval_mem_iff_coefficients U.toSubmodule A.coord).mpr hAU t` and `rw [dualTangentLinear_polynomialFirstJet_coord]; exact (eval_mem_iff_coefficients V _).mpr (directionalDerivative_mem_coefficientSubmodule V h A.coord hAV) t`.
findings.benefit: The proof no longer depends on writing out the unfolded form of polynomialFirstJetHom by hand. A single canonical rewrite then serves every place that needs the base or tangent value of a polynomial first jet.
